generalInformation.title: General Information
generalInformation.description: If you wish to take anaesthetics (e.g. strong-acting painkillers) with you on a trip abroad, a medical certificate is required in many cases. This must be certified by the responsible health authority before travelling.

regulationsSection.title: The regulations differ depending on the destination:

schengenStates.title: Schengen States:
schengenStates.description: A standardised certificate in accordance with Article 75 of the Schengen Convention is required.

otherCountries.title: Other countries
otherCountries.description: If you are travelling outside the Schengen area, you should inform yourself in advance about the national regulations of the respective destination or transit country. As a rule, a medical certificate with official certification is required.

certificateForm.downloadLabel: Medical Certificate Form for other countries

documentsSection.title: Required documents
documentsSection.description: For the certification by the public health department you need:

checklist.certificateFromDoctor: A completed medical certificate (depending on the destination)
checklist.personalIdentityDocument: A valid identity document (e.g. identity card or passport)

notice.title: Important
notice.description: Please note: A separate certificate must be submitted for each anaesthetic prescribed.

processingTimeSection.title: Processing time
processingTimeSection.description: As a rule, the certification can be carried out directly on the day of the appointment and you can take the certificate with you immediately.

appointmentsSection.title: Would you like to schedule an appointment?
appointmentsSection.description: Appointments for the certification can be arranged by telephone.
